name: Aenbarr
questions: Which part of the house is the self-contained one-bed flat: does it have its own entrance, kitchen and bathroom, and is it one of the six bedrooms or in addition to them? Can you send a floor plan?
The room list shows no bathroom on the first floor (Bedrooms Four to Six). Is there one, and where is the third bathroom the listing counts?

The house is BER G with 'central heating': what fuel and boiler, how old, and what insulation do the 1930s walls and the 1977 and 1986 extensions have? Is the BER certificate with the kWh/m²/yr figure available?
MyHome shows an earlier listing of Aenbarr marked Sale Agreed in June 2024. Why did that sale fall through, and did a survey find anything?
Is the house on mains water and mains sewer or a well and septic tank? BuyerIQ flags a High Radon Area: has a radon test been done? How much N11 traffic noise reaches the garden?

ai.why: A real fit for six plus the parents: 220 m², three ground-floor bedrooms (one en-suite) and a self-contained flat, on half an acre of mature trees at the foot of the Sugarloaf, about 7 km from the Bray DART. The 1930s cottage keeps its hipped slate roof and roughcast front, but the extensions are plain. At €725k, BER G (a rough €70–120k retrofit), no upstairs bathroom and the N11 about 450 m away pull it back to the baseline.

electricity.detail: Likely connected; not stated, but the house is lived in and the listing tags central heating.

water.detail: Unknown; not stated. Glencap Road is on the edge of Kilmacanogue village, so mains water is plausible; ask.

sewer.detail: Unknown; not stated whether it is on mains sewer or a septic tank; ask.

internet.detail: Full fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband — 388 Mb full fibre'); the listing doesn't mention broadband.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Three ground-floor bedrooms in the room list, including the master (4.73 × 3.31 m) with a 2.37 × 1.73 m en-suite, plus a family bathroom; there is also a self-contained one-bed flat in the original cottage with its own small rear garden. No floor plan is published.

bedsNote: Three bedrooms on the ground floor and three upstairs, plus two ground-floor office/TV rooms (4.09 × 2.89 m and 4.20 × 4.09 m) and a one-bed flat in the original cottage
tagline: A 1930s cottage extended into a 220 m² six-bed house, with a self-contained flat, on half an acre of mature trees at the foot of the Sugarloaf, just above Kilmacanogue village.

pros.text: Room for the parents on the ground floor, twice over
pros.detail: Three ground-floor bedrooms, the master (4.73 × 3.31 m) with an en-suite, beside a family bathroom; separately, a self-contained one-bed flat in the original cottage with its own small rear garden.

pros.text: Space for six: 220 m², six bedrooms
pros.detail: An 8.26 × 4.11 m living/dining room, a 5.39 × 5.07 m country kitchen, a 5.34 × 3.20 m conservatory and two more 12–17 m² office/TV rooms.

pros.text: Close to Dublin by DART and the N11
pros.detail: Bray Daly DART station about 7 km away; St Stephen's Green about 25 km by the N11 and M11, roughly 30–40 min off-peak; Greystones station is the other option.

pros.text: Half an acre of mature gardens under the Sugarloaf
pros.detail: About 0.5 ac (0.2 ha) behind gates, with a tree-lined gravel drive and lawns; the listing says the Sugarloaf walking trail starts from the driveway.
The original single-storey cottage keeps its hipped slate roof, chimneys, roughcast walls and a multi-pane window; the listing says it was owned by the Attorney General during WWII.
Kilmacanogue NS (St Mochonog's), mixed, 224 pupils, on Rocky Valley Crescent just north of the house; bus stops for the 45A, 131 and 133 about 560 m away.
BuyerIQ shows 388 Mb full fibre for A98 P268.

cons.detail: €225k over the ~€500k line and above the ~€700k ceiling for near-Dublin charm; €3,295/m², stamp duty about €7,250.

G means over 450 kWh/m²/yr. Insulating 1930s walls plus 1970s/80s extensions, new windows, airtightness and a heat pump on 220 m² is a rough €70–120k before SEAI grants (very rough; no survey), taking the total towards €800k+.
The room list puts both bathrooms (en-suite 2.37 × 1.73 m and family 2.39 × 1.44 m) on the ground floor; the three first-floor bedrooms (one only 2.34 × 2.30 m) have none listed.

cons.text: N11 dual carriageway about 450 m east
cons.detail: The Glen of the Downs dual carriageway passes Kilmacanogue roughly 450–500 m east (from map coordinates), carrying tens of thousands of vehicles a day; expect a background hum in the garden. Mature trees may help; listen on a viewing.
The 1977/1986 work adds a storey-and-a-half gabled wing and a flat-roofed brick link porch that don't match the cottage; only about 5 of 30 photos were viewable, none of the kitchen or conservatory.

CHI at Crumlin, about 30 km via the N11 and M50; Tallaght's children's unit is a 24/7 emergency care unit that sends the sickest children to Crumlin. St Vincent's takes adults only and Loughlinstown has no ED.

BuyerIQ puts it in an EPA High Radon Area and shows 10 planning applications within 1 km (one active build); water and drainage aren't stated; MyHome shows an earlier listing marked Sale Agreed in June 2024.

cons.text: Half an acre, not a full acre
cons.detail: About 0.5 ac of garden, smaller than the ~1 ac ideal for the dogs; neighbours' distance not checked from above.
